questions.stem: Which facility-security design best uses defense in depth?
options: Rely on one highly visible warning sign
Combine perimeter deterrence, controlled access, detection, response, and protected critical assets
Use cameras without monitoring or response
Issue identical access credentials to all visitors
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Layered security uses independent and complementary measures so failure of one control does not expose the entire facility.
incorrectOptionExplanations: One warning layer can be bypassed and provides no detection or response.
Unmonitored cameras may record an event but do not create timely intervention.
Uncontrolled credentials defeat identity, authorization, and accountability.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 32, physical security, access control, and facility protection, pp. 731-741

questions.stem: A contractor needs temporary access to one process area for two days. What is the strongest access-control approach?
options: Issue a permanent employee credential so access will not need further administration
Permit the contractor to use a host employee credential while accompanied in the area
Verify identity and need, issue limited access, brief the contractor, and recover the credential
Keep the controlled entrance unlocked during work hours so the contractor can enter freely
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Least-privilege access should be specific to the person, purpose, place, and duration, with logging and closure.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Permanent broad access exceeds the demonstrated need.
Shared credentials destroy accountability and may bypass authorization controls.
Propping a secure door exposes the area to uncontrolled entry.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 32, access control and employee control, pp. 733-735

questions.stem: What should a site-security risk assessment consider before choosing controls?
options: Only the price of fencing
Only the number of guards on day shift
Only incidents reported by nearby companies
Assets, credible threats, vulnerabilities, consequences, existing controls, and response capability
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Security controls should be risk-based and aligned with the assets and pathways that matter most to the facility.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Cost is evaluated after security needs and alternatives are understood.
Guard count is one existing control and does not define threats or vulnerabilities.
External history is useful but cannot replace site-specific analysis.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 32, site security plan and protection elements, pp. 731-741

questions.stem: Which visitor-control practice provides the strongest accountability?
options: Preauthorize the visit, verify identity, issue a visible limited badge, escort as required, and record exit
Ask visitors to sign a blank sheet
Permit unescorted access after a verbal introduction
Use employee badges for frequent visitors
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A complete visitor process controls identity, purpose, movement, sponsor responsibility, and credential recovery.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A blank sign-in sheet does not link identity, sponsor, destination, or time.
A verbal introduction does not establish controlled access and continuing accountability.
Employee credentials can grant excessive privileges and obscure visitor status.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 32, access control and employee control, pp. 733-735

questions.stem: A printed process diagram with emergency isolation points is left in a public lobby. What should be done?
options: Leave it because physical security and information security are unrelated
Remove it, evaluate the disclosure, and control sensitive operational information according to need and policy
Post more copies so employees can find it
Destroy every process diagram in the facility
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Security planning protects information that could expose critical assets while preserving authorized safety and operating access.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Sensitive information can enable physical intrusion or sabotage and requires coordinated protection.
More public copies increase uncontrolled disclosure.
Operational teams still need controlled access to accurate safety information.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 32, information security and equipment/facility protection, pp. 734-736

questions.stem: Unauthorized tailgating occurs repeatedly at a controlled entrance. Which response is strongest?
options: Send one reminder email and make no physical change
Disable the badge reader during busy periods
Improve entry design and authentication, train users, monitor events, and enforce the access process
Assume anyone following an employee is authorized
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Effective correction combines engineering, administrative, behavioral, and monitoring controls based on why tailgating occurs.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A reminder alone may not overcome throughput, layout, or detection weaknesses.
Disabling authentication removes the primary control.
Physical proximity is not proof of identity or authorization.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 32, physical security and access control, pp. 733-735

questions.stem: An unattended package with unusual wiring is found near a critical entrance. What is the best immediate action?
options: Move the package to an exterior location where it can be inspected away from employees
Open the package while wearing protective gloves to identify the owner and contents
Place the package in a covered waste container and continue normal entrance operations
Leave it undisturbed, isolate the area, and activate the emergency and security process
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Suspicious items should be left undisturbed while trained authorities evaluate them under the emergency plan.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Moving a suspicious item can trigger a device and exposes the handler.
Gloves do not protect against explosive or chemical hazards.
A trash container does not provide safe isolation and can spread consequences.

questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 32 and 39, site security and bomb-threat response, pp. 731-741 and 882-884

questions.stem: A security drill shows that an alarm is detected but no one knows who contacts law enforcement. What should follow?
options: Correct roles and communication procedures, retrain, and retest the response
Declare success because the alarm worked
Remove the alarm to avoid confusion
Keep the gap confidential and take no action
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Exercises validate the entire detection-to-response chain and should produce assigned, verified corrective actions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Detection without coordinated response is incomplete protection.
Removing detection weakens security and does not solve role ambiguity.
Uncorrected exercise findings remain real vulnerabilities.
